title: A Fish the Size of Your Finger Passed the Mirror Test

scenes.text: A fish as long as your finger passed a test most animals fail.
Scientists put a mirror in the tank of a bluestreak cleaner wrasse.
At first it attacked its reflection. Then it swam upside down in front of it.
Then researchers marked its throat with a brown gel, a spot only a mirror could show.
The fish scraped its throat on the sand, and several of them checked the mirror afterward.
Scientists still argue about what it proves, but the fish acted as if that reflection was itself.

description:
A fish as long as your finger passed the mirror test.
In 2019, Osaka researchers found that cleaner wrasses scraped a mark off their own throats, but only when a mirror let them see it.
Do you think a fish can know itself?
first_comment: Does passing the mirror test prove self-awareness? Tell us which animal to test next.
